page.description: Plugins add commands from trusted tools. They are downloaded from allowed GitHub repositories, and every file is checked against the release checksums before anything runs.
page.emptyDescription: Install one from the allowed repositories below.
page.availableDescription: Latest releases of the repositories in Sources.
page.nothingAvailable: Everything from the allowed repositories is installed.
page.sourcesDescription: GitHub repositories plugins may be installed from. A repository is checked before it is added: its latest release must hold a valid Canopy plugin.
page.noSources: No repository is allowed yet: plugins cannot be installed.
page.removeSourceDescription: Its releases will no longer be offered. A plugin already installed from it stays installed but can no longer be updated.
page.installedDescription: Each plugin has its own page: what its forms start with, the devices it finds, its commands, its version.

defaults.none: This plugin has no field to fill in advance.
defaults.label: Name for this value of {field}

detail.updateDescription: Its checksum is verified before anything is replaced; settings and devices stay.
detail.defaultsDescription: Fill in a field once and every form of this plugin starts with it. Add more values to offer a choice by name.
detail.devicesDescription: What this plugin finds on the network. Name them as people know them.
detail.commandsDescription: What this plugin adds to Canopy. Hidden ones are reached from where they belong (a pairing window).
detail.enabledHelp: Off, its commands disappear everywhere until you turn it back on.
detail.pinnedHelp: No update is offered while this is on.
detail.uninstallHelp: Removes the plugin, its commands and its data (pairings). Kept devices can then be forgotten.
detail.uninstallDescription: {name} and its commands leave Canopy. Running operations stop.
